L.7bt: ^17:10^ Inclinávit cælos, et descéndit: * et calígo sub pédibus eius.
L.7bv: ^17:11^ Et ascéndit super Chérubim, et volávit: * volávit super pennas ventórum.
L.7bx: ^17:12^ Et pósuit ténebras latíbulum suum, in circúitu eius tabernáculum eius: * tenebrósa aqua in núbibus áëris.
L.7bz: ^17:13^ Præ fulgóre in conspéctu eius nubes transiérunt, * grando et carbónes ignis.
L.7c1: ^17:14^ Et intónuit de cælo Dóminus, et Altíssimus dedit vocem suam: * grando et carbónes ignis.
L.7c3: ^17:15^ Et misit sagíttas suas, et dissipávit eos: * fúlgura multiplicávit, et conturbávit eos.
L.7c6: ^17:16^ Et apparuérunt fontes aquárum, * et reveláta sunt fundaménta orbis terrárum:
L.7c4: ^17:16^ Ab increpatióne tua, Dómine, * ab inspiratióne spíritus iræ tuæ.
L.7cz: ^17:2^ I will love thee, O Lord, my strength: * The Lord is my firmament, my refuge, and my deliverer.
L.7dn: ^17:3^ My God is my helper, * and in him will I put my trust.
L.7do: ^17:3^ My protector, and the horn of my salvation, * and my support.
L.7eb: ^17:4^ Praising, I will call upon the Lord: * and I shall be saved from my enemies.
L.7eh: ^17:5^ The sorrows of death surrounded me: * and the torrents of iniquity troubled me.
L.7ej: ^17:6^ The sorrows of hell encompassed me: * and the snares of death prevented me.
L.7em: ^17:7^ In my affliction I called upon the Lord, * and I cried to my God:
L.7ek: ^17:7^ And he heard my voice from his holy temple: * and my cry before him came into his ears.
L.7ep: ^17:8^ The earth shook and trembled: * the foundations of the mountains were troubled and were moved, because he was angry with them.
L.7er: ^17:9^ There went up a smoke in his wrath: and a fire flamed from his face: * coals were kindled by it.
L.7bs: ^17:10^ He bowed the heavens, and came down, * and darkness was under his feet.
L.7bu: ^17:11^ And he ascended upon the cherubim, and he flew; * he flew upon the wings of the winds.
L.7bw: ^17:12^ And he made darkness his covert, his pavilion round about him: * dark waters in the clouds of the air.
L.7by: ^17:13^ At the brightness that was before him the clouds passed, * hail and coals of fire.
L.7c0: ^17:14^ And the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Highest gave his voice: * hail and coals of fire.
L.7c2: ^17:15^ And he sent forth his arrows, and he scattered them: * he multiplied lightnings, and troubled them.
L.7c7: ^17:16^ Then the fountains of waters appeared, * and the foundations of the world were discovered:
L.7c5: ^17:16^ At thy rebuke, O Lord, * at the blast of the spirit of thy wrath.
L.7c9: ^17:17^ Misit de summo, et accépit me: * et assúmpsit me de aquis multis.
L.7ca: ^17:18^ Erípuit me de inimícis meis fortíssimis, et ab his qui odérunt me: * quóniam confortáti sunt super me.
L.7cc: ^17:19^ Prævenérunt me in die afflictiónis meæ: * et factus est Dóminus protéctor meus.
L.7cf: ^17:20^ Et edúxit me in latitúdinem: * salvum me fecit, quóniam vóluit me.
L.7ch: ^17:21^ Et retríbuet mihi Dóminus secúndum iustítiam meam: * et secúndum puritátem mánuum meárum retríbuet mihi:
L.7cj: ^17:22^ Quia custodívi vias Dómini, * nec ímpie gessi a Deo meo.
L.7cl: ^17:23^ Quóniam ómnia iudícia eius in conspéctu meo: * et iustítias eius non répuli a me.
L.7cn: ^17:24^ Et ero immaculátus cum eo: * et observábo me ab iniquitáte mea.
L.7cp: ^17:25^ Et retríbuet mihi Dóminus secúndum iustítiam meam: * et secúndum puritátem mánuum meárum in conspéctu oculórum eius.
L.7cq: ^17:26^ Cum sancto sanctus eris, * et cum viro innocénte ínnocens eris:
L.7ct: ^17:27^ Et cum elécto eléctus eris: * et cum pervérso pervertéris.
L.7cv: ^17:28^ Quóniam tu pópulum húmilem salvum fácies: * et óculos superbórum humiliábis.
L.7cx: ^17:29^ Quóniam tu illúminas lucérnam meam, Dómine: * Deus meus, illúmina ténebras meas.
L.7d1: ^17:30^ Quóniam in te erípiar a tentatióne, * et in Deo meo transgrédiar murum.
L.7d3: ^17:31^ Deus meus, impollúta via eius: elóquia Dómini igne examináta: * protéctor est ómnium sperántium in se.
L.7d5: ^17:32^ Quóniam quis Deus præter Dóminum? * aut quis Deus præter Deum nostrum?
L.7d6: ^17:33^ Deus, qui præcínxit me virtúte: * et pósuit immaculátam viam meam.
L.7d8: ^17:34^ Qui perfécit pedes meos tamquam cervórum, * et super excélsa státuens me.
L.7da: ^17:35^ Qui docet manus meas ad prǽlium: * et posuísti, ut arcum ǽreum, brácchia mea.
L.7c8: ^17:17^ He sent from on high, and took me: * and received me out of many waters.
L.7cb: ^17:18^ He delivered me from my strongest enemies, and from them that hated me: * for they were too strong for me.
L.7cd: ^17:19^ They prevented me in the day of my affliction: * and the Lord became my protector.
L.7ce: ^17:20^ And he brought me forth into a large place: * he saved me, because he was well pleased with me.
L.7cg: ^17:21^ And the Lord will reward me according to my justice; * and will repay me according to the cleanness of my hands:
L.7ci: ^17:22^ Because I have kept the ways of the Lord; * and have not done wickedly against my God.
L.7ck: ^17:23^ For all his judgments are in my sight: * and his justices I have not put away from me.
L.7cm: ^17:24^ And I shall be spotless with him: * and shall keep myself from my iniquity.
L.7co: ^17:25^ And the Lord will reward me according to my justice: * and according to the cleanness of my hands before his eyes.
L.7cr: ^17:26^ With the holy thou wilt be holy; * and with the innocent man thou wilt be innocent:
L.7cs: ^17:27^ And with the elect thou wilt be elect: * and with the perverse thou wilt be perverted.
L.7cu: ^17:28^ For thou wilt save the humble people; * but wilt bring down the eyes of the proud.
L.7cw: ^17:29^ For thou lightest my lamp, O Lord: * O my God, enlighten my darkness.
L.7d0: ^17:30^ For by thee I shall be delivered from temptation; * and through my God I shall go over a wall.
L.7d2: ^17:31^ As for my God, his way is undefiled: the words of the Lord are fire-tried: * he is the protector of all that trust in him.
L.7d4: ^17:32^ For who is God but the Lord? * or who is God but our God?
L.7d7: ^17:33^ God, who hath girt me with strength; * and made my way blameless.
L.7d9: ^17:34^ Who hath made my feet like the feet of harts: * and who setteth me upon high places.
L.7db: ^17:35^ Who teacheth my hands to war: * and thou hast made my arms like a brazen bow.
L.7dd: ^17:36^ Et dedísti mihi protectiónem salútis tuæ: * et déxtera tua suscépit me:
L.7de: ^17:36^ Et disciplína tua corréxit me in finem: * et disciplína tua ipsa me docébit.
L.7dg: ^17:37^ Dilatásti gressus meos subtus me: * et non sunt infirmáta vestígia mea:
L.7dj: ^17:38^ Pérsequar inimícos meos et comprehéndam illos: * et non convértar, donec defíciant.
L.7dk: ^17:39^ Confríngam illos, nec póterunt stare: * cadent subtus pedes meos.
L.7dr: ^17:40^ Et præcinxísti me virtúte ad bellum: * et supplantásti insurgéntes in me subtus me.
L.7dt: ^17:41^ Et inimícos meos dedísti mihi dorsum, * et odiéntes me disperdidísti.
L.7du: ^17:42^ Clamavérunt, nec erat qui salvos fáceret ad Dóminum: * nec exaudívit eos.
L.7dx: ^17:43^ Et commínuam eos, ut púlverem ante fáciem venti: * ut lutum plateárum delébo eos.
L.7dy: ^17:44^ Erípies me de contradictiónibus pópuli: * constítues me in caput géntium.
L.7e1: ^17:45^ Pópulus quem non cognóvi servívit mihi: * in audítu auris obedívit mihi.
L.7e2: ^17:46^ Fílii aliéni mentíti sunt mihi, * fílii aliéni inveteráti sunt, et claudicavérunt a sémitis suis.
L.7e5: ^17:47^ Vivit Dóminus, et benedíctus Deus meus: * et exaltétur Deus salútis meæ.
L.7e6: ^17:48^ Deus, qui das vindíctas mihi, et subdis pópulos sub me: * liberátor meus de inimícis meis iracúndis.
L.7e9: ^17:49^ Et ab insurgéntibus in me exaltábis me: * a viro iníquo erípies me.
L.7ec: ^17:50^ Proptérea confitébor tibi in natiónibus, Dómine: * et nómini tuo psalmum dicam.
L.7ef: ^17:51^ Magníficans salútes Regis eius, et fáciens misericórdiam Christo suo David: * et sémini eius usque in sǽculum.
L.7df: ^17:36^ Thou hast given me the protection of thy salvation: * and thy right hand hath held me up:
L.7dc: ^17:36^ And thy discipline hath corrected me unto the end: * and thy discipline, the same shall teach me.
L.7dh: ^17:37^ Thou hast enlarged my steps under me; * and my feet are not weakened.
L.7di: ^17:38^ I will pursue after my enemies, and overtake them: * and I will not turn again till they are consumed.
L.7dl: ^17:39^ I will break them, and they shall not be able to stand: * they shall fall under my feet.
L.7dq: ^17:40^ And thou hast girded me with strength unto battle; * and hast subdued under me them that rose up against me.
L.7ds: ^17:41^ And thou hast made my enemies turn their back upon me, * and hast destroyed them that hated me.
L.7dv: ^17:42^ They cried, but there was none to save them, to the Lord: * but he heard them not.
L.7dw: ^17:43^ And I shall beat them as small as the dust before the wind; * I shall bring them to nought, like the dirt in the streets.
L.7dz: ^17:44^ Thou wilt deliver me from the contradictions of the people; * thou wilt make me head of the Gentiles.
L.7e0: ^17:45^ A people which I knew not, hath served me: * at the hearing of the ear they have obeyed me.
L.7e3: ^17:46^ The children that are strangers have lied to me, * strange children have faded away, and have halted from their paths.
L.7e4: ^17:47^ The Lord liveth, and blessed be my God, * and let the God of my salvation be exalted.
L.7e7: ^17:48^ O God, who avengest me, and subduest the people under me, * my deliverer from my enraged enemies.
L.7e8: ^17:49^ And thou wilt lift me up above them that rise up against me: * from the unjust man thou wilt deliver me.
L.7ed: ^17:50^ Therefore will I give glory to thee, O Lord, among the nations, * and I will sing a psalm to thy name.
L.7ee: ^17:51^ Giving great deliverance to his king, and shewing mercy to David, his anointed: * and to his seed for ever.
L.q82: ^1^ Et vidi quod aperuísset Agnus unum de septem sigíllis, et audívi unum de quátuor animálibus, dicens tamquam vocem tonítrui: Veni, et vide.
L.r2l: ^2^ Et vidi: et ecce equus albus, et qui sedébat super illum, habébat arcum, et data est ei coróna, et exívit vincens ut vínceret.
L.rgt: ^3^ Et cum aperuísset sigíllum secúndum, audívi secúndum ánimal, dicens: Veni, et vide.
L.rv4: ^4^ Et exívit álius equus rufus: et qui sedébat super illum, datum est ei ut súmeret pacem de terra, et ut ínvicem se interfíciant, et datus est ei gládius magnus.
L.s8s: ^5^ Et cum aperuísset sigíllum tértium, audívi tértium ánimal, dicens: Veni, et vide. Et ecce equus niger: et qui sedébat super illum, habébat statéram in manu sua.
L.sin: ^6^ Et audívi tamquam vocem in médio quátuor animálium dicéntium: Bílibris trítici denário et tres bílibres hórdei denário, et vinum, et óleum ne lǽseris.
L.stb: ^7^ Et cum aperuísset sigíllum quartum, audívi vocem quarti animális dicéntis: Veni, et vide.
L.t2l: ^8^ Et ecce equus pállidus: et qui sedébat super eum, nomen illi Mors, et inférnus sequebátur eum, et data est illi potéstas super quátuor partes terræ, interfícere gládio, fame, et morte, et béstiis terræ.
L.7jw: ^36:1^ Noli æmulári in malignántibus: * neque zeláveris faciéntes iniquitátem.
L.7km: ^36:2^ Quóniam tamquam fænum velóciter aréscent: * et quemádmodum ólera herbárum cito décident.
L.7l7: ^36:3^ Spera in Dómino, et fac bonitátem: * et inhábita terram, et pascéris in divítiis eius.
L.7ld: ^36:4^ Delectáre in Dómino: * et dabit tibi petitiónes cordis tui.
L.7lj: ^36:5^ Revéla Dómino viam tuam, et spera in eo: * et ipse fáciet.
L.7lm: ^36:6^ Et edúcet quasi lumen iustítiam tuam: et iudícium tuum tamquam merídiem: * súbditus esto Dómino, et ora eum.
L.7lq: ^36:7^ Noli æmulári in eo, qui prosperátur in via sua: * in hómine faciénte iniustítias.
L.7lu: ^36:8^ Désine ab ira, et derelínque furórem: * noli æmulári ut malignéris.
L.7m0: ^36:9^ Quóniam qui malignántur, exterminabúntur: * sustinéntes autem Dóminum, ipsi hereditábunt terram.
L.7it: ^36:10^ Et adhuc pusíllum, et non erit peccátor: * et quæres locum eius et non invénies.
L.7j0: ^36:11^ Mansuéti autem hereditábunt terram: * et delectabúntur in multitúdine pacis.
L.7j3: ^36:12^ Observábit peccátor iustum: * et stridébit super eum déntibus suis.
L.7j7: ^36:13^ Dóminus autem irridébit eum: * quóniam próspicit quod véniet dies eius.
L.7j9: ^36:14^ Gládium evaginavérunt peccatóres: * intendérunt arcum suum,
L.7je: ^36:14^ Ut deíciant páuperem et ínopem: * ut trucídent rectos corde.
L.7jf: ^36:15^ Gládius eórum intret in corda ipsórum: * et arcus eórum confringátur.
L.7jt: ^36:1^ Be not emulous of evildoers; * nor envy them that work iniquity.
L.7kl: ^36:2^ For they shall shortly wither away as grass, * and as the green herbs shall quickly fall.
L.7l9: ^36:3^ Trust in the Lord, and do good, * and dwell in the land, and thou shalt be fed with its riches.
L.7le: ^36:4^ Delight in the Lord, * and he will give thee the requests of thy heart.
L.7lh: ^36:5^ Commit thy way to the Lord, and trust in him, * and he will do it.
L.7ll: ^36:6^ And he will bring forth thy justice as the light, and thy judgment as the noonday: * be subject to the Lord and pray to him.
L.7lp: ^36:7^ Envy not the man who prospereth in his way; * the man who doth unjust things.
L.7lt: ^36:8^ Cease from anger, and leave rage; * have no emulation to do evil.
L.7ly: ^36:9^ For the evildoers shall be cut off: * but they that wait upon the Lord shall inherit the land.
L.7iu: ^36:10^ For yet a little while, and the wicked shall not be: * and thou shalt seek his place, and shalt not find it.
L.7ix: ^36:11^ But the meek shall inherit the land, * and shall delight in abundance of peace.
L.7j4: ^36:12^ The sinner shall watch the just man: * and shall gnash upon him with his teeth.
L.7j6: ^36:13^ But the Lord shall laugh at him: * for he foreseeth that his day shall come.
L.7jc: ^36:14^ The wicked have drawn out the sword: * they have bent their bow.
L.7jd: ^36:14^ To cast down the poor and needy, * to kill the upright of heart.
L.7jh: ^36:15^ Let their sword enter into their own hearts, * and let their bow be broken.
L.7jl: ^36:16^ Mélius est módicum iusto, * super divítias peccatórum multas.
L.7jo: ^36:17^ Quóniam brácchia peccatórum conteréntur: * confírmat autem iustos Dóminus.
L.7jp: ^36:18^ Novit Dóminus dies immaculatórum: * et heréditas eórum in ætérnum erit.
L.7jr: ^36:19^ Non confundéntur in témpore malo, et in diébus famis saturabúntur: * quia peccatóres períbunt.
L.7jy: ^36:20^ Inimíci vero Dómini mox ut honorificáti fúerint et exaltáti: * deficiéntes, quemádmodum fumus defícient.
L.7jz: ^36:21^ Mutuábitur peccátor, et non solvet: * iustus autem miserétur et tríbuet.
L.7k2: ^36:22^ Quia benedicéntes ei hereditábunt terram: * maledicéntes autem ei disperíbunt.
L.7k3: ^36:23^ Apud Dóminum gressus hóminis dirigéntur: * et viam eius volet.
L.7k5: ^36:24^ Cum cecíderit non collidétur: * quia Dóminus suppónit manum suam.
L.7k8: ^36:25^ Iúnior fui, étenim sénui: * et non vidi iustum derelíctum, nec semen eius quærens panem.
L.7ka: ^36:26^ Tota die miserétur et cómmodat: * et semen illíus in benedictióne erit.
L.7kc: ^36:27^ Declína a malo, et fac bonum: * et inhábita in sǽculum sǽculi.
L.7kf: ^36:28^ Quia Dóminus amat iudícium, et non derelínquet sanctos suos: * in ætérnum conservabúntur.
L.7ke: ^36:28^ Iniústi puniéntur: * et semen impiórum períbit.
L.7ki: ^36:29^ Iusti autem hereditábunt terram: * et inhabitábunt in sǽculum sǽculi super eam.
L.7jj: ^36:16^ Better is a little to the just, * than the great riches of the wicked.
L.7jn: ^36:17^ For the arms of the wicked shall be broken in pieces; * but the Lord strengtheneth the just.
L.7jq: ^36:18^ The Lord knoweth the days of the undefiled; * and their inheritance shall be for ever.
L.7js: ^36:19^ They shall not be confounded in the evil time; and in the days of famine they shall be filled, * because the wicked shall perish.
L.7jx: ^36:20^ And the enemies of the Lord, presently after they shall be honoured and exalted, * shall come to nothing and vanish like smoke.
L.7k0: ^36:21^ The sinner shall borrow, and not pay again; * but the just sheweth mercy and shall give.
L.7k1: ^36:22^ For such as bless him shall inherit the land: * but such as curse him shall perish.
L.7k4: ^36:23^ With the Lord shall the steps of a man be directed, * and he shall like well his way.
L.7k6: ^36:24^ When he shall fall he shall not be bruised, * for the Lord putteth his hand under him.
L.7k7: ^36:25^ I have been young, and now am old; * and I have not seen the just forsaken, nor his seed seeking bread.
L.7k9: ^36:26^ He sheweth mercy, and lendeth all the day long; * and his seed shall be in blessing.
L.7kb: ^36:27^ Decline from evil and do good, * and dwell for ever and ever.
L.7kd: ^36:28^ For the Lord loveth judgment, and will not forsake his saints: * they shall be preserved for ever.
L.7kg: ^36:28^ The unjust shall be punished, * and the seed of the wicked shall perish.
L.7kh: ^36:29^ But the just shall inherit the land, * and shall dwell therein for evermore.
L.7kn: ^36:30^ Os iusti meditábitur sapiéntiam, * et lingua eius loquétur iudícium.
L.7kp: ^36:31^ Lex Dei eius in corde ipsíus, * et non supplantabúntur gressus eius.
L.7kr: ^36:32^ Consíderat peccátor iustum: * et quærit mortificáre eum.
L.7ku: ^36:33^ Dóminus autem non derelínquet eum in mánibus eius: * nec damnábit eum, cum iudicábitur illi.
L.7kw: ^36:34^ Exspécta Dóminum, et custódi viam eius: et exaltábit te ut hereditáte cápias terram: * cum períerint peccatóres vidébis.
L.7ky: ^36:35^ Vidi ímpium superexaltátum, * et elevátum sicut cedros Líbani.
L.7l0: ^36:36^ Et transívi, et ecce non erat: * et quæsívi eum, et non est invéntus locus eius.
L.7l1: ^36:37^ Custódi innocéntiam, et vide æquitátem: * quóniam sunt relíquiæ hómini pacífico.
L.7l4: ^36:38^ Iniústi autem disperíbunt simul: * relíquiæ impiórum interíbunt.
L.7l6: ^36:39^ Salus autem iustórum a Dómino: * et protéctor eórum in témpore tribulatiónis.
L.7lc: ^36:40^ Et adiuvábit eos Dóminus et liberábit eos: * et éruet eos a peccatóribus, et salvábit eos: quia speravérunt in eo.
L.7ko: ^36:30^ The mouth of the just shall meditate wisdom: * and his tongue shall speak judgment.
L.7kq: ^36:31^ The law of his God is in his heart, * and his steps shall not be supplanted.
L.7ks: ^36:32^ The wicked watcheth the just man, * and seeketh to put him to death.
L.7kt: ^36:33^ But the Lord will not leave him in his hands; * nor condemn him when he shall be judged.
L.7kv: ^36:34^ Expect the Lord and keep his way: and he will exalt thee to inherit the land: * when the sinners shall perish thou shalt see.
L.7kx: ^36:35^ I have seen the wicked highly exalted, * and lifted up like the cedars of Libanus.
L.7kz: ^36:36^ And I passed by, and lo, he was not: * and I sought him and his place was not found.
L.7l2: ^36:37^ Keep innocence, and behold justice: * for there are remnants for the peaceable man.
L.7l3: ^36:38^ But the unjust shall be destroyed together: * the remnants of the wicked shall perish.
L.7l5: ^36:39^ But the salvation of the just is from the Lord, * and he is their protector in the time of trouble.
L.7lb: ^36:40^ And the Lord will help them and deliver them: * and he will rescue them from the wicked, and save them, because they have hoped in him.
L.ckr: ^2^ Et vidi septem Ángelos stantes in conspéctu Dei: et datæ sunt illis septem tubæ.
L.cqm: ^3^ Et álius Ángelus venit, et stetit ante altáre habens thuríbulum áureum: et data sunt illi incénsa multa, ut daret de oratiónibus sanctórum ómnium super altáre áureum, quod est ante thronum Dei.
L.ct8: ^4^ Et ascéndit fumus incensórum de oratiónibus sanctórum de manu Ángeli coram Deo.
L.cvw: ^5^ Et accépit Ángelus thuríbulum, et implévit illud de igne altáris, et misit in terram: et facta sunt tonítrua, et voces, et fúlgura, et terræmótus magnus.
L.cyu: ^6^ Et septem Ángeli, qui habébant septem tubas, præparavérunt se ut tuba cánerent.
L.d14: ^7^ Et primus Ángelus tuba cécinit, et facta est grando, et ignis, mista in sánguine, et missum est in terram.
L.d18: ^7^ Et tértia pars terræ combústa est, et tértia pars árborum concremáta est, et omne fœnum víride combústum est.
L.d44: ^8^ Et secúndus Ángelus tuba cécinit: et tamquam mons magnus igne ardens missus est in mare, et facta est tértia pars maris sanguis,
L.d65: ^9^ Et mórtua est tértia pars creatúræ eórum, quæ habébant ánimas in mari, et tértia pars návium intériit.
L.7od: ^48:2^ Audíte hæc, omnes gentes: * áuribus percípite omnes, qui habitátis orbem:
L.7og: ^48:3^ Quique terrígenæ, et fílii hóminum: * simul in unum dives et pauper.
L.7oi: ^48:4^ Os meum loquétur sapiéntiam: * et meditátio cordis mei prudéntiam.
L.7ok: ^48:5^ Inclinábo in parábolam aurem meam: * apériam in psaltério propositiónem meam.
L.7ol: ^48:6^ Cur timébo in die mala? * iníquitas calcánei mei circúmdabit me:
L.7on: ^48:7^ Qui confídunt in virtúte sua: * et in multitúdine divitiárum suárum gloriántur.
L.7op: ^48:8^ Frater non rédimit, rédimet homo: * non dabit Deo placatiónem suam.
L.7or: ^48:9^ Et prétium redemptiónis ánimæ suæ: * et laborábit in ætérnum, et vivet adhuc in finem.
L.7nq: ^48:11^ Non vidébit intéritum, cum víderit sapiéntes moriéntes: * simul insípiens, et stultus períbunt.
L.7no: ^48:11^ Et relínquent aliénis divítias suas: * et sepúlcra eórum domus illórum in ætérnum.
L.7nr: ^48:12^ Tabernácula eórum in progénie et progénie: * vocavérunt nómina sua in terris suis.
L.7nu: ^48:13^ Et homo, cum in honóre esset, non intelléxit: * comparátus est iuméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
L.7oe: ^48:2^ Hear these things, all ye nations: * give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world.
L.7of: ^48:3^ All you that are earthborn, and you sons of men: * both rich and poor together.
L.7oh: ^48:4^ My mouth shall speak wisdom: * and the meditation of my heart understanding.
L.7oj: ^48:5^ I will incline my ear to a parable; * I will open my proposition on the psaltery.
L.7om: ^48:6^ Why shall I fear in the evil day? * the iniquity of my heel shall encompass me.
L.7oo: ^48:7^ They that trust in their own strength, * and glory in the multitude of their riches,
L.7oq: ^48:8^ No brother can redeem, nor shall man redeem: * he shall not give to God his ransom,
L.7os: ^48:9^ Nor the price of the redemption of his soul: * and shall labour for ever, and shall still live unto the end.
L.7np: ^48:11^ He shall not see destruction, when he shall see the wise dying: * the senseless and the fool shall perish together:
L.7nn: ^48:11^ And they shall leave their riches to strangers: * and their sepulchres shall be their houses for ever.
L.7ns: ^48:12^ Their dwelling places to all generations: * they have called their lands by their names.
L.7nt: ^48:13^ And man when he was in honour did not understand; * he is compared to senseless beasts, and is become like to them.
L.7nv: ^48:14^ Hæc via illórum scándalum ipsis: * et póstea in ore suo complacébunt.
L.7nz: ^48:15^ Sicut oves in inférno pósiti sunt: * mors depáscet eos.
L.7ny: ^48:15^ Et dominabúntur eórum iusti in matutíno: * et auxílium eórum veteráscet in inférno a glória eórum.
L.7o2: ^48:16^ Verúmtamen Deus rédimet ánimam meam de manu ínferi: * cum accéperit me.
L.7o4: ^48:17^ Ne timúeris, cum dives factus fúerit homo: * et cum multiplicáta fúerit glória domus eius.
L.7o6: ^48:18^ Quóniam cum interíerit, non sumet ómnia: * neque descéndet cum eo glória eius.
L.7o8: ^48:19^ Quia ánima eius in vita ipsíus benedicétur: * confitébitur tibi cum beneféceris ei.
L.7oa: ^48:20^ Introíbit usque in progénies patrum suórum: * et usque in ætérnum non vidébit lumen.
L.7ob: ^48:21^ Homo, cum in honóre esset, non intelléxit: * comparátus est iuméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
L.7nw: ^48:14^ This way of theirs is a stumbling block to them: * and afterwards they shall delight in their mouth.
L.7o0: ^48:15^ They are laid in hell like sheep: * death shall feed upon them.
L.7nx: ^48:15^ And the just shall have dominion over them in the morning; * and their help shall decay in hell from their glory.
L.7o1: ^48:16^ But God will redeem my soul from the hand of hell, * when he shall receive me.
L.7o3: ^48:17^ Be not thou afraid, when a man shall be made rich, * and when the glory of his house shall be increased.
L.7o5: ^48:18^ For when he shall die he shall take nothing away; * nor shall his glory descend with him.
L.7o7: ^48:19^ For in his lifetime his soul will be blessed: * and he will praise thee when thou shalt do well to him.
L.7o9: ^48:20^ He shall go in to the generations of his fathers: * and he shall never see light.
L.7oc: ^48:21^ Man when he was in honour did not understand: * he hath been compared to senseless beasts, and made like to them.
L.cei: ^1^ Et vidi álium Ángelum fortem descendéntem de cælo amíctum nube, et iris in cápite eius, et fácies eius erat ut sol, et pedes eius tamquam colúmnæ ignis:
L.ckm: ^2^ Et habébat in manu sua libéllum apértum: et pósuit pedem suum dextrum super mare, sinístrum autem super terram:
L.cq5: ^3^ Et clamávit voce magna, quemádmodum cum leo rugit. Et cum clamásset, locúta sunt septem tonítrua voces suas.
L.cej: ^1^ Et vidi álium Ángelum fortem descendéntem de cælo amíctum nube, et iris in cápite ejus, et fácies ejus erat ut sol, et pedes ejus tamquam colúmnæ ignis:
L.ctf: ^4^ Et cum locúta fuíssent septem tonítrua voces suas, ego scriptúrus eram: et audívi vocem de cælo dicéntem mihi: Signa quæ locúta sunt septem tonítrua: et noli ea scríbere.
L.cwc: ^5^ Et Ángelus, quem vidi stantem super mare et super terram, levávit manum suam ad cælum:
L.cyq: ^6^ Et iurávit per vivéntem in sǽcula sæculórum, qui creávit cælum, et ea quæ in eo sunt: et terram, et ea quæ in ea sunt: et mare, et ea quæ in eo sunt: Quia tempus non erit ámplius.
L.cyr: ^6^ Et jurávit per vivéntem in sǽcula sæculórum, qui creávit cælum, et ea quæ in eo sunt: et terram, et ea quæ in ea sunt: et mare, et ea quæ in eo sunt: Quia tempus non erit ámplius.
L.d2a: ^7^ Sed in diébus vocis séptimi Ángeli, cum cœ́perit tuba cánere, consummábitur mystérium Dei sicut evangelizávit per servos suos prophétas.
L.d3t: ^8^ Et audívi vocem de cælo íterum loquéntem mecum, et dicéntem: Vade, et áccipe librum apértum de manu Ángeli stantis super mare, et super terram.
L.d68: ^9^ Et ábii ad Ángelum, dicens ei, ut daret mihi librum.
L.7qg: ^67:2^ Exsúrgat Deus, et dissipéntur inimíci eius, * et fúgiant qui odérunt eum, a fácie eius.
L.7qh: ^67:2^ Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered: * and let them that hate him flee from before his face.
L.cea: ^1^ Et datus est mihi cálamus símilis virgæ, et dictum est mihi: Surge, et metíre templum Dei, et altáre, et adorántes in eo:
L.cm1: ^2^ Átrium autem, quod est foris templum, éice foras, et ne metiáris illud: quóniam datum est géntibus, et civitátem sanctam calcábunt ménsibus quadragínta duóbus:
L.cq6: ^3^ Et dabo duóbus téstibus meis, et prophetábunt diébus mille ducéntis sexagínta, amícti saccis.
L.ctx: ^4^ Hi sunt duæ olívæ et duo candelábra in conspéctu Dómini terræ stantes.
L.cw8: ^5^ Et si quis volúerit eos nocére, ignis éxiet de ore eórum, et devorábit inimícos eórum: et si quis volúerit eos lǽdere, sic opórtet eum occídi.
L.cz6: ^6^ Hi habent potestátem claudéndi cælum, ne pluat diébus prophetíæ ipsórum: et potestátem habent super aquas converténdi eas in sánguinem, et percútere terram omni plaga quotiescúmque volúerint.
L.d0z: ^7^ Et cum finíerint testimónium suum, béstia, quæ ascéndit de abýsso, fáciet advérsum eos bellum, et vincet illos, et occídet eos.
L.7tp: ^77:32^ In ómnibus his peccavérunt adhuc: * et non credidérunt in mirabílibus eius.
L.7tr: ^77:33^ Et defecérunt in vanitáte dies eórum: * et anni eórum cum festinatióne.
L.7ts: ^77:34^ Cum occíderet eos, quærébant eum: * et revertebántur, et dilúculo veniébant ad eum.
L.7tv: ^77:35^ Et rememoráti sunt quia Deus adiútor est eórum: * et Deus excélsus redémptor eórum est.
L.7tx: ^77:36^ Et dilexérunt eum in ore suo, * et lingua sua mentíti sunt ei.
L.7tz: ^77:37^ Cor autem eórum non erat rectum cum eo: * nec fidéles hábiti sunt in testaménto eius.
L.7u3: ^77:38^ Ipse autem est miséricors, et propítius fiet peccátis eórum: * et non dispérdet eos.
L.7u2: ^77:38^ Et abundávit ut avérteret iram suam: * et non accéndit omnem iram suam:
L.7u5: ^77:39^ Et recordátus est quia caro sunt: * spíritus vadens et non rédiens.
L.7u9: ^77:40^ Quóties exacerbavérunt eum in desérto, * in iram concitavérunt eum in inaquóso?
L.7ub: ^77:41^ Et convérsi sunt, et tentavérunt Deum: * et Sanctum Israël exacerbavérunt.
L.7to: ^77:32^ In all these things they sinned still: * and they believed not for his wondrous works.
L.7tq: ^77:33^ And their days were consumed in vanity, * and their years in haste.
L.7tt: ^77:34^ When he slew them, then they sought him: * and they returned, and came to him early in the morning.
L.7tu: ^77:35^ And they remembered that God was their helper: * and the most high God their redeemer.
L.7tw: ^77:36^ And they loved him with their mouth: * and with their tongue they lied unto him:
L.7ty: ^77:37^ But their heart was not right with him: * nor were they counted faithful in his covenant.
L.7u1: ^77:38^ But he is merciful, and will forgive their sins: * and will not destroy them.
L.7u0: ^77:38^ And many a time did he turn away his anger: * and did not kindle all his wrath.
L.7u4: ^77:39^ And he remembered that they are flesh: * a wind that goeth and returneth not.
L.7u8: ^77:40^ How often did they provoke him in the desert: * and move him to wrath in the place without water?
L.7ua: ^77:41^ And they turned back and tempted God: * and grieved the holy one of Israel.
L.7uc: ^77:42^ Non sunt recordáti manus eius, * die qua redémit eos de manu tribulántis.
L.7uf: ^77:43^ Sicut pósuit in Ægýpto signa sua, * et prodígia sua in campo Táneos.
L.7uh: ^77:44^ Et convértit in sánguinem flúmina eórum: * et imbres eórum, ne bíberent.
L.7uj: ^77:45^ Misit in eos cœnomyíam, et comédit eos: * et ranam, et dispérdidit eos.
L.7ul: ^77:46^ Et dedit ærúgini fructus eórum: * et labóres eórum locústæ.
L.7un: ^77:47^ Et occídit in grándine víneas eórum: * et moros eórum in pruína.
L.7up: ^77:48^ Et trádidit grándini iuménta eórum: * et possessiónem eórum igni.
L.7ur: ^77:49^ Misit in eos iram indignatiónis suæ: * indignatiónem, et iram, et tribulatiónem: immissiónes per ángelos malos.
L.7ux: ^77:50^ Viam fecit sémitæ iræ suæ, non pepércit a morte animábus eórum: * et iuménta eórum in morte conclúsit.
L.7uz: ^77:51^ Et percússit omne primogénitum in terra Ægýpti: * primítias omnis labóris eórum in tabernáculis Cham.
L.7v1: ^77:52^ Et ábstulit sicut oves pópulum suum: * et perdúxit eos tamquam gregem in desérto.
L.7v3: ^77:53^ Et dedúxit eos in spe, et non timuérunt: * et inimícos eórum opéruit mare.
L.7v7: ^77:54^ Et indúxit eos in montem sanctificatiónis suæ: * montem, quem acquisívit déxtera eius.
L.7v6: ^77:54^ Et eiécit a fácie eórum gentes: * et sorte divísit eis terram in funículo distributiónis.
L.7v9: ^77:55^ Et habitáre fecit in tabernáculis eórum: * tribus Israël.
L.7va: ^77:56^ Et tentavérunt, et exacerbavérunt Deum excélsum: * et testimónia eius non custodiérunt.
L.7vd: ^77:57^ Et avertérunt se, et non servavérunt pactum: * quemádmodum patres eórum convérsi sunt in arcum pravum.
L.7ve: ^77:58^ In iram concitavérunt eum in cóllibus suis: * et in sculptílibus suis ad æmulatiónem eum provocavérunt.
L.7ud: ^77:42^ They remembered not his hand, * in the day that he redeemed them from the hand of him that afflicted them:
L.7ue: ^77:43^ How he wrought his signs in Egypt, * and his wonders in the field of Tanis.
L.7ug: ^77:44^ And he turned their rivers into blood, * and their showers that they might not drink.
L.7ui: ^77:45^ He sent amongst them diverse sorts of flies, which devoured them: * and frogs which destroyed them.
L.7uk: ^77:46^ And he gave up their fruits to the blast, * and their labours to the locust.
L.7um: ^77:47^ And he destroyed their vineyards with hail, * and their mulberry trees with hoarfrost.
L.7uo: ^77:48^ And he gave up their cattle to the hail, * and their stock to the fire.
L.7uq: ^77:49^ And he sent upon them the wrath of his indignation: * indignation and wrath and trouble, which he sent by evil angels.
L.7uw: ^77:50^ He made a way for a path to his anger: * he spared not their souls from death, and their cattle he shut up in death.
L.7uy: ^77:51^ And he killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt: * the firstfruits of all their labour in the tabernacles of Cham.
L.7v0: ^77:52^ And he took away his own people as sheep: * and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.
L.7v2: ^77:53^ And he brought them out in hope, and they feared not: * and the sea overwhelmed their enemies.
L.7v4: ^77:54^ And he brought them into the mountain of his sanctuary: * the mountain which his right hand had purchased.
L.7v5: ^77:54^ And he cast out the Gentiles before them: * and by lot divided to them their land by a line of distribution.
L.7v8: ^77:55^ And he made the tribes of Israel * to dwell in their tabernacles.
L.7vb: ^77:56^ Yet they tempted, and provoked the most high God: * and they kept not his testimonies.
L.7vc: ^77:57^ And they turned away, and kept not the covenant: * even like their fathers they were turned aside as a crooked bow.
L.7vf: ^77:58^ They provoked him to anger on their hills: * and moved him to jealousy with their graven things.
L.7vg: ^77:59^ Audívit Deus, et sprevit: * et ad níhilum redégit valde Israël.
L.7vn: ^77:60^ Et répulit tabernáculum Silo: * tabernáculum suum, ubi habitávit in homínibus.
L.7vp: ^77:61^ Et trádidit in captivitátem virtútem eórum: * et pulchritúdinem eórum in manus inimíci.
L.7vr: ^77:62^ Et conclúsit in gládio pópulum suum: * et hereditátem suam sprevit.
L.7vt: ^77:63^ Iúvenes eórum comédit ignis: * et vírgines eórum non sunt lamentátæ.
L.7vu: ^77:64^ Sacerdótes eórum in gládio cecidérunt: * et víduæ eórum non plorabántur.
L.7vx: ^77:65^ Et excitátus est tamquam dórmiens Dóminus: * tamquam potens crapulátus a vino.
L.7vz: ^77:66^ Et percússit inimícos suos in posterióra: * oppróbrium sempitérnum dedit illis.
L.7w1: ^77:67^ Et répulit tabernáculum Ioseph: * et tribum Éphraim non elégit.
L.7w3: ^77:68^ Sed elégit tribum Iuda, * montem Sion quem diléxit.
L.7w5: ^77:69^ Et ædificávit sicut unicórnium sanctifícium suum in terra, * quam fundávit in sǽcula.
L.7w9: ^77:70^ Et elégit David, servum suum, et sústulit eum de grégibus óvium: * de post fœtántes accépit eum,
L.7wa: ^77:71^ Páscere Iacob, servum suum, * et Israël, hereditátem suam:
L.7wd: ^77:72^ Et pavit eos in innocéntia cordis sui: * et in intelléctibus mánuum suárum dedúxit eos.
L.7vh: ^77:59^ God heard, and despised them, * and he reduced Israel exceedingly as it were to nothing.
L.7vm: ^77:60^ And he put away the tabernacle of Silo, * his tabernacle where he dwelt among men.
L.7vo: ^77:61^ And he delivered their strength into captivity: * and their beauty into the hands of the enemy.
L.7vq: ^77:62^ And he shut up his people under the sword: * and he despised his inheritance.
L.7vs: ^77:63^ Fire consumed their young men: * and their maidens were not lamented.
L.7vv: ^77:64^ Their priests fell by the sword: * and their widows did not mourn.
L.7vw: ^77:65^ And the Lord was awaked as one out of sleep, * and like a mighty man that hath been surfeited with wine.
L.7vy: ^77:66^ And he smote his enemies on the hinder parts: * he put them to an everlasting reproach.
L.7w0: ^77:67^ And he rejected the tabernacle of Joseph: * and chose not the tribe of Ephraim:
L.7w2: ^77:68^ But he chose the tribe of Juda, * mount Sion which he loved.
L.7w4: ^77:69^ And he built his sanctuary as of unicorns, in the land * which he founded for ever.
L.7w8: ^77:70^ And he chose his servant David, and took him from the flocks of sheep: * he brought him from following the ewes great with young,
L.7wb: ^77:71^ To feed Jacob his servant, * and Israel his inheritance.
L.7wc: ^77:72^ And he fed them in the innocence of his heart: * and conducted them by the skilfulness of his hands.

L.70o: ^105:1^ Confitémini Dómino, quóniam bonus: * quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia eius.
L.718: ^105:2^ Quis loquétur poténtias Dómini, * audítas fáciet omnes laudes eius?
L.71q: ^105:3^ Beáti, qui custódiunt iudícium, * et fáciunt iustítiam in omni témpore.
L.72c: ^105:4^ Meménto nostri, Dómine, in beneplácito pópuli tui: * vísita nos in salutári tuo:
L.72e: ^105:5^ Ad vidéndum in bonitáte electórum tuórum, ad lætándum in lætítia gentis tuæ: * ut laudéris cum hereditáte tua.
L.72g: ^105:6^ Peccávimus cum pátribus nostris: * iniúste égimus, iniquitátem fécimus.
L.72l: ^105:7^ Patres nostri in Ægýpto non intellexérunt mirabília tua: * non fuérunt mémores multitúdinis misericórdiæ tuæ.
L.72j: ^105:7^ Et irritavérunt ascendéntes in mare, * Mare Rubrum.
L.72n: ^105:8^ Et salvávit eos propter nomen suum: * ut notam fáceret poténtiam suam.
L.72p: ^105:9^ Et incrépuit Mare Rubrum, et exsiccátum est, * et dedúxit eos in abýssis sicut in desérto.
L.705: ^105:10^ Et salvávit eos de manu odiéntium: * et redémit eos de manu inimíci.
L.707: ^105:11^ Et opéruit aqua tribulántes eos: * unus ex eis non remánsit.
L.709: ^105:12^ Et credidérunt verbis eius: * et laudavérunt laudem eius.
L.70a: ^105:13^ Cito fecérunt, oblíti sunt óperum eius: * et non sustinuérunt consílium eius.
L.70d: ^105:14^ Et concupiérunt concupiscéntiam in desérto: * et tentavérunt Deum in inaquóso.
L.70f: ^105:15^ Et dedit eis petitiónem ipsórum: * et misit saturitátem in ánimas eórum.
L.70p: ^105:1^ Give glory to the Lord, for he is good: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
L.719: ^105:2^ Who shall declare the powers of the Lord? * who shall set forth all his praises?
L.71r: ^105:3^ Blessed are they that keep judgment, * and do justice at all times.
L.72d: ^105:4^ Remember us, O Lord, in the favour of thy people: * visit us with thy salvation.
L.72f: ^105:5^ That we may see the good of thy chosen, that we may rejoice in the joy of thy nation: * that thou mayst be praised with thy inheritance.
L.72h: ^105:6^ We have sinned with our fathers: * we have acted unjustly, we have wrought iniquity.
L.72k: ^105:7^ Our fathers understood not thy wonders in Egypt: * they remembered not the multitude of thy mercies:
L.72i: ^105:7^ And they provoked to wrath going up to the sea, * even the Red Sea.
L.72m: ^105:8^ And he saved them for his own name’s sake: * that he might make his power known.
L.72o: ^105:9^ And he rebuked the Red Sea, and it was dried up: * and he led them through the depths, as in a wilderness.
L.704: ^105:10^ And he saved them from the hand of them that hated them: * and he redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.
L.706: ^105:11^ And the water covered them that afflicted them: * there was not one of them left.
L.708: ^105:12^ And they believed his words: * and they sang his praises.
L.70b: ^105:13^ They had quickly done, they forgot his works: * and they waited not for his counsels.
L.70c: ^105:14^ And they coveted their desire in the desert: * and they tempted God in the place without water.
L.70e: ^105:15^ And he gave them their request: * and sent fulness into their souls.
L.70h: ^105:16^ Et irritavérunt Móysen in castris: * Aaron, sanctum Dómini.
L.70i: ^105:17^ Apérta est terra, et deglutívit Dathan: * et opéruit super congregatiónem Abíron.
L.70l: ^105:18^ Et exársit ignis in synagóga eórum * flamma combússit peccatóres.
L.70m: ^105:19^ Et fecérunt vítulum in Horeb * et adoravérunt scúlptile.
L.70r: ^105:20^ Et mutavérunt glóriam suam * in similitúdinem vítuli comedéntis fænum.
L.70s: ^105:21^ Oblíti sunt Deum, qui salvávit eos, * qui fecit magnália in Ægýpto, mirabília in terra Cham: terribília in Mari Rubro.
L.70v: ^105:23^ Et dixit ut dispérderet eos: * si non Móyses, eléctus eius, stetísset in confractióne in conspéctu eius:
L.70x: ^105:24^ Ut avérteret iram eius ne dispérderet eos: * et pro níhilo habuérunt terram desiderábilem:
L.70y: ^105:25^ Non credidérunt verbo eius, et murmuravérunt in tabernáculis suis: * non exaudiérunt vocem Dómini.
L.711: ^105:26^ Et elevávit manum suam super eos: * ut prostérneret eos in desérto:
L.713: ^105:27^ Et ut deíceret semen eórum in natiónibus: * et dispérgeret eos in regiónibus.
L.714: ^105:28^ Et initiáti sunt Beélphegor: * et comedérunt sacrifícia mortuórum.
L.717: ^105:29^ Et irritavérunt eum in adinventiónibus suis: * et multiplicáta est in eis ruína.
L.71a: ^105:30^ Et stetit Phínees, et placávit: * et cessávit quassátio.
L.71d: ^105:31^ Et reputátum est ei in iustítiam: * in generatiónem et generatiónem usque in sempitérnum.
L.70g: ^105:16^ And they provoked Moses in the camp, * Aaron the holy one of the Lord.
L.70j: ^105:17^ The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan: * and covered the congregation of Abiron.
L.70k: ^105:18^ And a fire was kindled in their congregation: * the flame burned the wicked.
L.70n: ^105:19^ They made also a calf in Horeb: * and they adored the graven thing.
L.70q: ^105:20^ And they changed their glory * into the likeness of a calf that eateth grass.
L.70t: ^105:21^ They forgot God, who saved them, * who had done great things in Egypt, wondrous works in the land of Cham: terrible things in the Red Sea.
L.70u: ^105:23^ And he said that he would destroy them: * had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach:
L.70w: ^105:24^ To turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy them; * and they set at nought the desirable land.
L.70z: ^105:25^ They believed not his word, and they murmured in their tents: * they hearkened not to the voice of the Lord.

L.aba: In illo témpore: Dixit Iesus discípulis suis: Módicum, et iam non vidébitis me; et íterum módicum, et vidébitis me: quia vado ad Patrem. Et réliqua.
L.ar8: Módicum est hoc totum spátium, quo præsens pérvolat sǽculum. Unde dicit idem ipse Evangelísta in Epístola sua: Novíssima hora est. Ideo namque áddidit: Quia vado ad Patrem: quod ad priórem senténtiam referéndum est, ubi ait: Módicum et iam non vidébitis me: non ad posteriórem, ubi ait: Et íterum módicum, et vidébitis me. Eúndo quippe ad Patrem, factúrus erat ut eum non vidérent.
L.975: At that time, Jesus said to his disciples: A little while, and now you shall not see me; and again a little while, and you shall see me: because I go to the Father. And so on.
L.bl7: This little while is the whole duration of this present world. In the same sense this same Evangelist saith in his Epistle ^ii. 18^: It is the last time. The words, because I go to the Father, refer to the first clause of the text, namely, A little while and ye shall not see Me, and not to the latter clause, that is, and again a little while, and ye shall see Me. By His going to the Father He was about to bring it to pass that they should see Him no more.
L.a7m: Illis ergo ait: Módicum, et iam non vidébitis me; qui eum corporáliter tunc vidébant: quia itúrus erat ad Patrem, et eum deínceps mortálem visúri non erant, qualem, cum ista loquerétur, vidébant. Quod vero áddidit: Et íterum módicum, et vidébitis me: univérsæ promísit Ecclésiæ, sicut univérsæ promísit: Ecce ego vobíscum sum usque ad consummatiónem sǽculi. Non tardat Dóminus promíssum.
L.a2s: He saith: A little while, and ye shall not see Me, a little while, and they who now saw Him clad in a dying nature, should see Him so no more, because He was about to go to the Father. But He saith: And again a little while, and ye shall see Me, and these words are a promise to the Universal Church, just as are those others: Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world ^Matth. xxviii. 20.^ Our Lord delayeth not His promised coming.
L.ar9: Módicum et vidébimus eum: ubi iam nihil rogémus, nihil interrogémus, quia nihil desiderándum remanébit, nihil quæréndum latébit. Hoc módicum longum nobis vidétur, quóniam adhuc ágitur; cum finítum fúerit, tunc sentiémus quam módicum fúerit. Non ergo sit gáudium nostrum quale habet mundus, de quo dictum est: Mundus autem gaudébit. Nec tamen in huius desidérii parturitióne sine gáudio tristes simus: sed, sicut ait Apóstolus: Spe gaudéntes.
L.91d: Again a little while, and we shall see Him. We shall see Him. And, O, when we shall see Him, then we shall beg, we shall ask no more; for no desire will be unsatisfied, and no riddle unsolved. This little while seemeth a very long while to us now, while as it is still going on, but when it is over we shall feel indeed how truly it is but a little while. Therefore, may our rejoicing never be like the rejoicing of that world whereof it is said: The world shall rejoice..

L.kob: In festo Virginis praedicanda est virginitas. Hoc in isto sermone suscepimus. Adiuvet Christus Virginis Filius et Virginum sponsus: virginali utero corporalitæ natus, virginali connubio spiritualiter coniugatus. L.iik: Ansélmus, Augústæ Prætóriæ in fínibus Itáliæ, nobílibus et cathólicis paréntibus natus, adoléscens, pátria et bonis ómnibus derelíctis, in monastério Beccénsi órdinis sancti Benedícti emíssa regulári professióne, in lítteris et virtútibus assequéndis mirum in modum profécit. Régibus, epíscopis veneratióni fuit, et sancto Gregório séptimo étiam accéptus, qui tunc, persecutiónibus agitátus, lítteras amóris plenas ad eum dedit, se et Ecclésiam eius oratiónibus comméndans. Defúncto Lanfránco archiepíscopo Cantuariénsi, eius olim præceptóre, ad eiúsdem ecclésiæ régimen vocátus, verbo et exémplo, scriptis et concíliis celebrátis, prístinam pietátem et ecclesiásticam disciplínam redúxit. Sed cum mox Willélmus rex vi et minis iura Ecclésiæ usurpáre tentásset, ípseque invícte restitísset, bonórum direptiónem et exsílium passus, Romam ad Urbánum secúndum se cóntulit. A quo honorífice excéptus et summis láudibus ornátus, in Barénsi concílio Spíritum Sanctum étiam a Fílio procedéntem, contra Græcórum errórem, innúmeris Scripturárum et sanctórum Patrum testimóniis propugnávit. L.iij: Anselm, born of noble Catholic parents at Aosta on the borders of Italy, as a young man abandoned his homeland and all his possessions and was professed at the Benedictine monastery of Bec, where he advanced in a most wonderful way in the attainment of learning and virtue. He was held in honour by kings and bishops, and was a friend of St. Gregory VII, at the time much troubled by persecutions, who wrote him letters filled with affection, commending himself and the Church to Anselm's prayers. After the death of Lanfranc, Archbishop of Canterbury and Anselm's former teacher, he was called to rule over that Church, and, by word and example, by writings and by holding councils, he restored it to its pristine state of piety and ecclesiastical discipline. But, soon after, when King William tried by force and threats to usurp the rights of the Church and Anselm steadfastly resisted, his possessions were confiscated and he himself exiled. He went to Urban II in Rome, who welcomed him with honour and the highest praise. At the Council of Bari, he defended against the errors of the Greeks the doctrine that the Holy Ghost proceedeth also from the Son, by countless proofs taken from the Scriptures and the holy Fathers. After King William's death, his brother Henry recalled Anselm to England, and there he fell asleep in the Lord.

L.mhz: Paulus a Cruce, Uvádæ in Ligúria natus, a primo ratiónis usu, Iesu Christi crucifíxi amóre flagrávit. Martýrii desidério incénsus, exercítui se adiúnxit, qui Venétiis ad bellum Turcis inferéndum comparabátur. Cógnita vero Dei voluntáte, honestíssimis núptiis sibíque deláta pátrui hereditáte recusátis, rudi túnica a suo epíscopo indútus, nondum cléricus, Domínicum agrum divíni verbi prædicatióne excóluit. Romæ a Summo Pontífice Benedícto décimo tértio ex obediéntia sacerdótio auctus, in solitúdinem recéssit Argentárii montis, quo eum beáta Virgo iamprídem invitáverat, veste illi simul osténsa atri colóris passiónis Fílii sui insígnibus decoráta, ibíque fundaménta iecit novæ congregatiónis, cuius sodáles voto adstringeréntur Domínicæ passiónis memóriam promovéndi. Sacras Vírgines quoque instítuit, quæ Dómini passiónem sédulo meditaréntur. Prædicatióne, virtútibus et divínis charismátibus clarus, Romæ obdormívit in Dómino, anno millésimo septingentésimo septuagésimo quinto. Eum Pius nonus Póntifex máximus in Beatórum, dein in Sanctórum númerum rétulit.
L.mhv: Paul of the Cross was born at Ovada in Liguria and, as soon as he came to the use of reason, burned with love for Jesus Christ crucified. Fired with the desire for martyrdom, he joined the army which was being assembled in Venice to fight against the Turks. But when the will of God was made known to him, and he had refused a most honourable marriage and an inheritance left to him by his uncle, he received a coarse tunic as a habit from his bishop and, although not yet a cleric, cultivated the field of the Lord by preaching the word of God. In Rome, out of obedience to Pope Benedict XIII, he was raised to the priesthood. Then he retired into the solitude of Monte Argentario, where the Blessed Virgin had already invited him to go, at the same time shewing unto him a black habit adorned with the insignia of her Son's Passion. There he laid the foundations of a new congregation, whose members bind themselves by vow to promote the memory of the Lord's Passion, and he also established one for nuns to meditate continually upon this mystery. Renowned for his preaching, virtues, and divine charisms, he fell asleep in the Lord at Rome, in the year 1775. Pope Pius IX enrolled him among the Blessed and then among the Saints.

L.mko: Pontífices et pharisǽi sibi consulébant: nec tamen dicébant: Credámus. Plus enim pérditi hómines cogitábant, quómodo nocérent, ut pérderent, quam quómodo sibi consúlerent, ne perírent: et tamen timébant, et quasi consulébant. Dicébant enim: Quid fácimus, quia hic homo multa signa facit? Si dimíttimus eum sic, omnes credent in eum: et vénient Románi, et tollent nostrum locum et gentem.
L.inh: At that time, chief priests and the Pharisees gathered a council, and said: What do we, for this man doth many miracles? If we let him alone so, all will believe in him; and the Romans will come, and take away our place and nation. And so on.
L.nwz: The chief Priests and the Pharisees took counsel together, but Let us believe in Him was not one of the suggestions offered. Those lost creatures thought much more how they might hurt and undo Him, than how they might save themselves from perishing. And yet they were afraid, and took counsel together, and said What do we? For this Man doeth many miracles. If we let Him thus alone, all men will believe on Him; and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and our nation.
L.nsk: Temporália pérdere timuérunt, et vitam ætérnam non cogitavérunt, ac sic utrúmque amisérunt. Nam et Románi post Dómini passiónem et glorificatiónem tulérunt eis et locum et gentem, expúgnando et transferéndo: et illud eos séquitur, quod álibi dictum est: Fílii autem regni huius ibunt in ténebras exterióres. Hoc autem timuérunt, ne, si omnes in Christum créderent, nemo remanéret, qui advérsus Romános civitátem Dei templúmque defénderet: quóniam contra ipsum templum, et contra suas patérnas leges doctrínam Christi esse sentiébant.
L.o1d: They were afraid of losing temporal things, but they gave no thought to eternal life, and so they lost both. For, after that the Lord had suffered and been glorified, first came the Romans, and took away both their place and nation, prevailing against them and leading them away captive, and secondly there followeth them that which is written But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness. ^Matth. viii. 12.^ But their fear was that, if all men should believe on Christ, none would remain to defend the city of God and His Temple against the Romans, since they deemed that Christ's teaching was against the Temple itself, and against the laws of their fathers.
L.obd: Unus autem ex ipsis Cáiphas, cum esset Póntifex anni illíus, dixit eis: Vos nescítis quidquam, nec cogitátis, quia éxpedit vobis ut unus moriátur homo pro pópulo, et non tota gens péreat. Hoc autem a semetípso non dixit: sed cum esset póntifex anni illíus, prophetávit. Hic docémur, étiam hómines malos prophetíæ spíritu futúra prædícere: quod tamen Evangelísta divíno tríbuit sacraménto, quia póntifex fuit, id est summus sacérdos.
L.igj: And one of them, named Ca'iphas, being the High Priest that same year, said unto them: Ye know nothing at all, nor consider that it is expedient for us that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not. And this spake he not of himself but being High Priest that year, he prophesied. Here we will learn that bad men are enabled by the spirit of prophecy to foretell the future; which, at the same time, the Evangelist attributeth to an ordinance of God, namely, that he was the High Priest.
L.6w3: We beseech thee, O Lord, pour thy grace into our hearts, that all we who of our own will do check our sins with the curb of mortification, may suffer here, and escape condemnation to eternal punishment hereafter.

L.cez: ^1^ Let a man so account of us as of the ministers of Christ, and the dispensers of the mysteries of God.
L.cl0: ^2^ Here now it is required among the dispensers, that a man be found faithful.
L.cpt: ^3^ But to me it is a very small thing to be judged by you, or by man's day; but neither do I judge my own self.
L.ctu: ^4^ For I am not conscious to myself of any thing, yet am I not hereby justified; but he that judgeth me, is the Lord.
L.cxa: ^5^ Therefore judge not before the time; until the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts; and then shall every man have praise from God.
L.8nu: * Be ye, therefore, wise as serpents and simple as doves, alleluia.
L.fou: ^℟.^ Be ye, therefore, wise as serpents and simple as doves, alleluia.
L.cz9: ^6^ Hæc autem, fratres, transfigurávi in me et Apóllo, propter vos: ut in nobis discátis, ne supra quam scriptum est, unus advérsus álterum inflétur pro álio.
L.d24: ^7^ Quis enim te discérnit? Quid autem habes quod non accepísti? Si autem accepísti, quid gloriáris quasi non accéperis?
L.d4g: ^8^ Iam saturáti estis, iam dívites facti estis: sine nobis regnátis: et útinam regnétis, ut et nos vobíscum regnémus.
L.d6s: ^9^ Puto enim quod Deus nos Apóstolos novíssimos osténdit, tamquam morti destinátos: quia spectáculum facti sumus mundo, et Ángelis, et homínibus.

L.d1d: ^7^ For who distinguisheth thee? Or what hast thou that thou hast not received? And if thou hast received, why dost thou glory, as if thou hadst not received it?
L.d56: ^8^ You are now full; you are now become rich; you reign without us; and I would to God you did reign, that we also might reign with you.
L.d6b: ^9^ For I think that God hath set forth us apostles, the last, as it were men appointed to death: we are made a spectacle to the world, and to angels, and to men.
L.8rp: * For my yoke is sweet and my burden light, alleluia.

L.c35: ^10^ Nos stulti propter Christum, vos autem prudéntes in Christo: nos infírmi, vos autem fortes: vos nóbiles, nos autem ignóbiles.
L.c55: ^11^ Usque in hanc horam et esurímus, et sitímus, et nudi sumus, et cólaphis cǽdimur, et instábiles sumus,
L.c5u: ^12^ Et laborámus operántes mánibus nostris: maledícimur, et benedícimus: persecutiónem pátimur, et sustinémus:
L.c72: ^13^ Blasphemámur, et obsecrámus: tamquam purgaménta huius mundi facti sumus, ómnium peripséma usque adhuc.
L.c8q: ^14^ Non ut confúndam vos, hæc scribo, sed ut fílios meos caríssimos móneo.
L.c9w: ^15^ Nam si decem míllia pædagogórum habeátis in Christo, sed non multos patres, nam in Christo Iesu per Evangélium ego vos génui.

L.c4k: ^11^ Even unto this hour we both hunger and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and have no fixed abode;
L.c5d: ^12^ And we labour, working with our own hands: we are reviled, and we bless; we are persecuted, and we suffer it.
L.c7v: ^13^ We are blasphemed, and we entreat; we are made as the refuse of this world, the offscouring of all even until now.
L.c8n: ^14^ I write not these things to confound you; but I admonish you as my dearest children.
L.c9r: ^15^ For if you have ten thousand instructors in Christ, yet not many fathers. For in Christ Jesus, by the gospel, I have begotten you.

L.jtd: Ex libro sancti Hierónymi Presbýteri de Scriptóribus ecclesiásticis
L.li4: Marcus, discípulus et intérpres Petri, iuxta quod Petrum referéntem audíerat, rogátus Romæ a frátribus, breve scripsit Evangélium. Quod cum Petrus audísset, et probávit, et Ecclésiæ legéndum sua auctoritáte dedit. Assúmpto ítaque Evangélio quod ipse confécerat, perréxit in Ægýptum, et primus Alexandríæ Christum annúntians, constítuit ecclésiam tanta doctrína et vitæ continéntia, ut omnes sectatóres Christi ad exémplum sui cógeret.
L.8td: * Isti sunt viri sancti facti amíci Dei, allelúia.
L.g2y: ^℟.^ Isti sunt viri sancti facti amíci Dei, allelúia.
L.k1t: From the Book upon Church Writers, composed by St. Jerome, Priest at Bethlehem.
L.li7: Mark was the disciple and interpreter of Peter, and it was from what he had heard Peter tell, that, at the request of the brethren at Rome, he wrote the shortest of the Gospels. When Peter had heard it, he approved it, and gave it to the Church to be read, by his authority. Mark betook himself to Egypt, with the Gospel which he had compiled, and was the first man who preached Christ at Alexandria. There he founded a Church with such teaching and austerity of life, that all who followed Christ were constrained to imitate him.
L.8xe: * These men are holy, for they are the friends of God, alleluia.
L.gek: ^℟.^ These men are holy, for they are the friends of God, alleluia.
L.jne: Dénique Philo, disertíssimus Iudæórum, videns Alexandríæ primam ecclésiam adhuc iudaizántem, quasi in laudem gentis suæ, librum super eórum conversatióne scripsit. Et quómodo Lucas narrat Ierosólymæ credéntes ómnia habuísse commúnia: sic et ille, quod Alexandríæ sub Marco fíeri doctóre cernébat, memóriæ trádidit. Mórtuus est autem octávo Nerónis anno, et sepúltus Alexandríæ, succedénte sibi Aniáno.
L.8u2: * Modo coronántur, et accípiunt palmam, allelúia.
L.g4p: ^℟.^ Modo coronántur, et accípiunt palmam, allelúia.
L.l9a: Last of all, Philo, that most learned Jew, observing that the first Church of Alexandria still kept the law of Moses, wrote a book concerning their manners, as if in praise of his own nation, wherein he saith that under the teaching of Mark, the Christians of Alexandria had all things in common, just as Luke telleth us was the case with all them that believed at Jerusalem. Mark died in the eighth year of Nero, and was buried at Alexandria. Anianus succeeded him.
L.8my: * And now have they crowns on their heads, and palms in their hands, alleluia.
L.fmr: ^℟.^ And now have they crowns on their heads, and palms in their hands, alleluia.
L.j9r: De Expositióne sancti Gregórii Papæ super Ezechiélem Prophétam
L.n8u: Sancta quátuor animália, quæ prophetíæ spíritu futúra prævidéntur, subtíli narratióne describúntur, cum dícitur: Quátuor fácies uni, et quátuor pennæ uni. Quid per fáciem, nisi notítia; et quid per pennas, nisi volátus exprímitur? Per fáciem quippe unusquísque cognóscitur: per pennas vero in altum ávium córpora sublevántur. Fácies ítaque ad fidem pértinet, penna ad contemplatiónem. Per fidem namque ab omnipoténti Deo cognóscimur, sicut ipse de suis óvibus dicit: Ego sum pastor bonus, et cognósco oves meas, et cognóscunt me meæ. Qui rursus ait: Ego scio quos elégerim. Per contemplatiónem vero, qua super nosmetípsos tóllimur, quasi in áëra levámur.
L.8vf: * Qui in patiéntia vestra possidébitis ánimas vestras, allelúia.
L.g8o: ^℟.^ Qui in patiéntia vestra possidébitis ánimas vestras, allelúia.
L.k20: From the Exposition of the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel by Pope St. Gregory ^the Great.^
L.nwc: The Prophet writeth very minutely touching the four holy living creatures, whom he saw in the spirit as being to come. He saith: “Every one had four faces, and every one had four wings.” What signifieth the face save likeness whereby we are known? or wings, save the power to fly since it is by the face that man is known from man, and by their wings that the birds' bodies are carried up into the air. So the face pertaineth to certitude, and the wings to contemplation. With certitude we are known of God Almighty, Who saith: “I am the Good Shepherd, and know My sheep, and am known of Mine.” ^John x. 14.^ And again: “I know whom I have chosen.” ^xiii. 18.^ And by contemplation, whereby we rise above ourselves, we as it were fly heavenwards.
L.8ve: * Qui in patiéntia vestra possidébitis ánimas vestras, alleluia.
L.g8n: ^℟.^ Qui in patiéntia vestra possidébitis ánimas vestras, alleluia.
L.kqv: In illo témpore: Dixit Petrus ad Iesum: Ecce nos relíquimus ómnia, et secúti sumus te: quid ergo erit nobis? Et réliqua.
L.k62: Grandis fidúcia! Petrus piscátor erat, dives non fúerat, cibos manu et arte quærébat: et tamen lóquitur confidénter: Relíquimus ómnia. Et quia non súfficit tantum relínquere, iungit quod perféctum est: Et secúti sumus te. Fécimus quod iussísti: quid ígitur nobis dabis prǽmii? Iesus autem dixit illis: Amen dico vobis, quod vos qui secúti estis me, in regeneratióne, cum séderit Fílius hóminis in sede maiestátis suæ, sedébitis et vos super sedes duódecim, iudicántes duódecim tribus Ísraël. Non dixit: Qui reliquístis ómnia; hoc enim et Crates fecit philósophus, et multi álii divítias contempsérunt: sed, Qui secúti estis me: quod próprie Apostolórum est, atque credéntium.
L.8w0: * Quorum doctrína fulget Ecclésia, ut sole luna, allelúia.
L.g9j: ^℟.^ Quorum doctrína fulget Ecclésia, ut sole luna, allelúia.
L.inb: At that time, Peter said unto Jesus: Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed thee what shall we have therefore? And so on.
L.mjs: Peter was a fisherman, he was not rich, he earned his bread by his hand and skill, and nevertheless he is thus bold, and saith confidently: We have forsaken all. And because it sufficeth not to forsake only, he addeth that which to do is to be perfect: and followed thee. We have done that which Thou hast commanded us, what reward therefore wilt Thou give us? And Jesus said unto them Amen I say unto you, that ye which have followed Me, in the regeneration, when the Son of Man shall sit in the throne of His glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. He said not, Ye which have forsaken all, for this did even Crates the philosopher, and they which have set nothing by riches are many, but, Ye which have followed Me. This did the Apostles, and this do believers do.
L.8o0: * By the light of whose teaching the Church is glorified, even as the moon is glorified by the light of the sun, alleluia.
L.fq0: ^℟.^ By the light of whose teaching the Church is glorified, even as the moon is glorified by the light of the sun, alleluia.
L.ktq: In regeneratióne, cum séderit Fílius hóminis in sede maiestátis suæ (quando et mórtui de corruptióne resúrgent incorrúpti) sedébitis et vos in sóliis iudicántium, condemnántes duódecim tribus Ísraël: quia vobis credéntibus, illi crédere noluérunt. Et omnis qui relíquerit domum, vel fratres, aut soróres, aut patrem, aut matrem, aut uxórem, aut fílios, aut agros propter nomen meum, céntuplum accípiet, et vitam ætérnam possidébit. Locus iste cum illa senténtia cóngruit, in qua Salvátor lóquitur: Non veni pacem míttere, sed gládium. Veni enim separáre hóminem a patre suo, et matrem a fília, et nurum a socru: et inimíci hóminis doméstici eius. Qui ergo propter fidem Christi, et prædicatiónem Evangélii, omnes afféctus contémpserint, atque divítias et sǽculi voluptátes: isti céntuplum recípient, et vitam ætérnam possidébunt.
L.8ql: * Et quasi colúmbæ ad fenéstras suas, allelúia.
L.fwb: ^℟.^ Et quasi colúmbæ ad fenéstras suas, allelúia.
L.kv0: In the regeneration, when the Son of Man shall sit in the throne of His glory, and when the dead shall rise again from corruption incorruptible, ^i Cor. xv. 53,^ ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones of judgment, condemning the twelve tribes of Israel, because, when ye believed in Me, they would not. ^John iii. 18.^ And every one that hath forsaken houses, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for My Name's sake, shall receive an hundredfold, and shall inherit everlasting life. This place agreeth well with that other where the Saviour saith I came not to send peace, but a sword. For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; and a man's foes shall be they of his own household. ^Matth. x. 34.^ Every one, therefore, that hath set no store by affection, and riches, and the pleasures of the world, for Christ's faith's sake, and the preaching of the Gospel, shall receive an hundred-fold, and shall inherit everlasting life.
L.8mn: * And as doves to their windows, alleluia.
L.fm8: ^℟.^ And as doves to their windows, alleluia.
L.jtg: Ex occasióne huius senténtiæ quidam introdúcunt mille annos post resurrectiónem, dicéntes, tunc nobis céntuplum ómnium rerum quas dimísimus, et vitam ætérnam esse reddéndam: non intelligéntes, quod, si in céteris digna sit repromíssio, in uxóribus appáreat turpitúdo: ut qui unam pro Dómino dimíserit centum recípiat in futúro. Sensus ergo iste est: Qui carnália pro Salvatóre dimíserit, spirituália recípiet: quæ comparatióne et mérito sui ita erunt, quasi si parvo número centenárius númerus comparétur.
L.iz2: By reason of these words, an hundredfold, some will have that there shall be a thousand years after the resurrection, wherein they that have forsaken all things shall receive an hundredfold of those things which they have forsaken, and shall inherit everlasting life. Such men consider not that though in other things this were worthy, as touching wives it is unseemly for it becometh us not to think that he that hath forsaken one wife in this world, shall receive an hundred wives in that which is to come. But the meaning is this, that every one that for the Saviour's sake hath forsaken earthly things, shall receive spiritual things which things, being rightly weighed against earthly things, are as though an hundredfold were weighed against one.
L.6h6: Deus, qui beátum Marcum Evangelístam tuum evangélicæ prædicatiónis grátia sublimásti: tríbue, quǽsumus; eius nos semper et eruditióne profícere et oratióne deféndi.
L.6pp: O God, Who didst exalt thy blessed Evangelist Mark, by giving him grace to preach thine Evangel, grant unto us, we beseech thee, ever to follow more and more what he teacheth, and ever to be shielded from all evil by his prayers.
